chunks: So have We revealed to you the Qur'an by Our command. You did not know what the Scripture was before, nor (the laws of) faith. And We made it a light by which We show the way to those of Our creatures as We please; and you certainly guide them to the right path,

key_terms.أَمْرِنَا: Our command, referring to God's decree or instruction
key_terms.الْإِيمَانُ: Faith, referring to belief in divine laws and tenets
key_terms.الْكِتَابُ: The Book, referring to the Qur'an or divine scripture
key_terms.رُوحًا: Spirit or soul, often referring to the Qur'an or divine inspiration
key_terms.صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ: Straight path, the direct way to God

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Ruh and Amr in the context of Quranic revelation?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the Prophet's (SAWW) human nature prior to revelation, emphasizing that his knowledge of the Book and Faith was purely divine bestowal rather than innate. The term 'Ruh' (Spirit) is often interpreted as the Qur'an itself or the divine essence of revelation, underscoring that while the Prophet guides humanity to the straight path, the ultimate source of guidance remains God's will. This distinction reinforces the concept of Wahy as a specific divine act that transformed the Prophet from a non-scholar into the perfect exemplar of faith.
